answer: Complete workflow finished: solution.py (deterministic, verified by clean re-run) produces all 18 required artifacts. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the approved plan: my plan-stage analysis had used V^T y (right-singular basis) for the "Fourier coefficients" — the correct Picard coefficients are U^T y (left-singular basis). Re-running everything with the correct basis changes two confirmed numbers: noise_estimate = 0.028875 (not 0.134) and effective_rank = 24 (not 14). The qualitative conclusions survive: noise is white Gaussian (re-verified: chi2 quantiles, KS p=0.113, flat autocorrelation, flat periodogram), dpc_judgment = does_not_hold, and — now clearly — the data are signal-dominated in the head (95.8% of data power in the first 26 singular directions; max component SNR 3180x), not noise-dominated. Your discrepancy convention applied exactly as specified: delta = min(sigma_hat*sqrt(n), 1.05*||y||) = 0.430225; the Tikhonov residual is monotonically increasing in alpha, so "smallest alpha whose residual meets the target" is the unique crossing, alpha* = 3.272002e-03 (bisection, residual = 0.430225 = delta). picard_data.csv uses the signed raw coefficient U^T y and picard_ratio = |coeff|/s_i, 222 rows; the report documents that the ratio's tail divergence (coefficients flat at the noise floor, s_i -> 0) re-estimates sigma. Methods (all parameters from data alone): A/Tikhonov alpha* = 3.272002e-3 by discrepancy principle (GCV cross-check 4.04e-4; L-curve smooth, no knee) — residual 0.430225 (= delta, at the noise level), ||x|| = 3.556; B/TSVD k = 24 = #{s_i > sigma_hat} — residual 0.417152 (tail-noise level), ||x|| = 5.159; C/CGLS k = 24 (effective-rank fallback) — residual 1.818597, ||x|| = 0.187. CGLS primary rules are all degenerate on this K and documented as such: the discrepancy target is never reached because the iteration STALLS (residual 1.8186 at k=24, 1.7735 at k=100, 1.7733 at k=222 = exact-arithmetic convergence limit; after 222 iterations it has captured only ~14% of the leading Fourier coefficient — K^T K has condition number ~3.3e29, so double-precision CGLS loses Krylov orthogonality), GCV-over-iterations is flat (residual monotonically decreasing), and the iteration L-curve has no knee. Recommendation by the documented data-only rule (rule justification + residual consistency + cross-method head agreement): method A Tikhonov — it fits exactly to the data-estimated noise level, retains ~95-99% of the strongly significant head components (i = 1,2,4,5,8,9,10,13) with correct shrinkage toward the edge of the information level (i = 16..24, where sigma/s_i is O(0.3-1) and unregularized estimates are noise-inflated), and agrees with the independent TSVS solution (correlation 0.858 over 99%-significant components, 0.896 over the full head); TSVS is the close second (hard cutoff, unshrunk edge components); CGLS is not trustworthy here. Uncertainties carried into the comparison report: single-realization white-noise assumption; edge-of-information-level coefficient uncertainty (i ~ 16..26); marginal components (i = 12, 16, 22, 26) possibly chance fluctuations; CGLS stalling is a floating-point limitation of the method, not of the data; effective-rank threshold sensitivity (24 vs 19 at 2*sigma).
